institutionName: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The most important aspect was UNC Chapel Hill’s strong academic profile, especially the Gillings School of Global Public Health. I chose UNC because Gillings is ranked among the very best public and global health schools in the United States, which made it highly relevant to my academic interests and future career goals. The course selection, academic environment, and opportunity to study public health at a leading institution were therefore crucial factors in my decision.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I really enjoyed my time at UNC Chapel Hill, especially the opportunity to meet new people and experience student life there. However, Chapel Hill is a relatively small town, which slightly limited the opportunities to explore different places nearby.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy to find the information I needed before and upon arrival. UNC provided clear and useful information in advance, including two online meetings before arrival, which helped prepare me well.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Before the semester started, there was an in-person orientation meeting on campus. This was helpful for getting practical information, understanding campus life, and meeting other international students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There were many different on-campus housing options to choose from. It was a bit expensive, but it was a convenient option, especially when arriving in a new city and wanting to live close to campus.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There were different meal plans available, which could be used at the two dining halls on campus. In the dorms, there were generally limited cooking facilities, usually only a small shared kitchen where students had to bring or buy their own kitchen equipment. The on-campus apartments had better cooking facilities, but they were also more expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Future exchange students should consider buying a meal plan, as cooking options in the dorms are limited. I would also recommend getting a small dorm fridge for the room, so you can keep drinks, snacks, and small food items there.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Your campus housing experience may also depend a lot on your roommate, since you usually share a room with another student.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Check in at Orientation meeting

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I had an academic advisor who I could contact for advice about the registration process, course selection, and how to register for classes.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was successful in registering for the classes I wanted. The process was not always completely straightforward, but in the end I was able to get the courses that were most relevant to me.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would recommend contacting the professors responsible for the courses directly by email, especially if you really want to take a specific course. The official registration process is not always very fast, and sometimes requests may not go through immediately. It is also a good idea to ask your academic advisor for help, as they can guide you through the registration process and advise you on what to do.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I only took Master's level courses at the highest academic level (700+ courses) This was not necessary in order to meet the 30 ECTS requirement, but I chose these courses because they sounded interesting and relevant to my studies. The academic level was high, but still manageable, and I found it possible to follow the courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style was different from UCPH. At UNC, there was more continuous work during the semester, including attendance, homework, quizzes, and assignments. However, as an exchange student, I only needed to pass the courses in order to transfer the credits to UCPH, so it was possible to prioritize which assignments to spend the most time on. Overall, it was not too difficult to keep up, and I quickly got used to studying and learning in English.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
I was enrolled only in the professional school, the Gillings School of Global Public Health. I took three courses of 3 credits each, which corresponded to 30 ECTS at UCPH:

HPM 725: Health Care Strategy and Marketing
HPM 766: Making Equity a Priority in Health Care Quality
PUBH 766: Implementation Science for Health Care Practice

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would also recommend taking an LFIT course, which is a physical activity course. Even though it may not be transferred to UCPH, it is a good opportunity to meet new people and try something different. I would also recommend considering a creative class, for example pottery, as UNC offers many different types of courses outside your main academic field. However, it is important to register quickly, as these courses can fill up fast.

questions.answer: Make plans to go sightseeing, specially springbreak

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of my exchange experience was the overall experience itself. I chose to go on exchange not only for the academic opportunities, but also to try something new, live in another country, meet new people, and experience a different university culture. Looking back, the most valuable part was stepping out of my usual environment and getting the chance to experience everyday student life at UNC Chapel Hill.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was deciding to go abroad in the first place and leaving my usual environment behind. However, once I arrived and settled in, I found it much easier than expected to live and study at UNC Chapel Hill.
